stem.text: The derivative of a function f is given by \( f'(x) = -\left(x - 3\right)^{2} \left(x - 4\right) \left(x^{2} + 1\right) \) for all x. Does f have a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at x = 3? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: f has neither a relative minimum nor a relative maximum at x = 3, because f' does not change sign at x = 3.

worked_solution.text: The factor \( \left(x - 3\right)^{2} \) makes \( f'(3) = 0 \), so x = 3 is a critical point of f.

The factor \( \left(x - 3\right)^{2} \) is never negative and every other factor is positive near x = 3, so \( f' \) does not change sign at x = 3. By the first derivative test f has neither a relative minimum nor a relative maximum there.

options.label: f has a relative minimum at x = 3, because f' takes its smallest nearby value at x = 3.
options.derivation: the classification taken from the value of f', which is smallest at the input, rather than from a change of sign

options.label: f has a relative maximum at x = 3, because f' is positive before and equal to 0 at x = 3.
options.derivation: a critical point with no sign change declared a relative maximum because f rises up to it
